content.overview: Articles 14 to 18 are the equality cluster. Article 14 is equality before the law and equal protection for any person. Article 15 prohibits the State from discriminating against citizens on religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, and restricts disability, liability, restriction or condition in access to listed public places on those grounds. It permits special provisions for women and children, for socially and educationally backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, for their admission to educational institutions, and economically weaker sections. Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment and authorises reservations in the terms of clauses (4), (4A), (4B) and (6). Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its enforcement an offence. Article 18 abolishes titles and restricts titles from a foreign State and titles used as name prefixes by State holders.
content.study: Use Article 14 for the general plea, Article 15 for the listed grounds and public access, Article 16 for State employment, Article 17 for untouchability, and Article 18 for titles. Do not merge them into one test.

enhancement.definition: The equality cluster is Articles 14 to 18: general equality, non-discrimination, public employment, abolition of untouchability, and abolition of titles.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Each article has its own beneficiary and its own exception. A special provision authorised by Article 15 or 16 is not pleaded as a bare Article 14 violation.
essentialIngredients: Citizen status checked for Articles 15 and 16
Special-provision clause checked before invalidating a reservation
Article 17 offence distinguished from a civil exclusion
Article 18 title distinguished from military or academic distinction
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 15(1) is a State discrimination ban on five grounds and applies to citizens. Article 15(2) reaches other persons for access to shops, public restaurants, hotels and places of public entertainment, and to wells, tanks, roads and places of public resort maintained wholly or partly out of State funds or dedicated to the public. Clauses (3) to (6) are enabling special provisions, including educational institutions and economically weaker sections. Article 16 is limited to employment or appointment under the State. Clause (4) is reservation for backward classes not adequately represented. Clause (4A) is consequential seniority in promotion. Clause (4B) concerns carry-forward and the fifty-percent ceiling's relationship, which is case-law and is not applied as a number here. Clause (6) is the economically weaker section reservation. Article 17 abolishes untouchability and its enforcement in any form. Article 18 prohibits State titles, with a military or academic distinction excluded from the ban on acceptance, and restricts foreign titles and honour prefixes.
examples: A State university denies admission on religion. Article 15(1) is the citizen's plea.
A State service rule reserves posts for a backward class. Article 16(4) is the enabling clause, not an automatic violation.
A person is excluded from a public well as untouchable. Article 17 applies, and Article 15(2) may also apply.
enhancement.problemApplication: Pick the article by subject: general equality, listed ground, public job, untouchability, or title. Check citizenship where the article requires it.
